gap: No result ChatGPT got says that Anker sells a single-cart, grid-charged whole-home kit ($7,399: SOLIX E10 + Power Dock + Smart Generator 5500). In that kit the battery starts the tri-fuel generator by itself when charge falls to a level you set. The generator refills the battery through a 4,500 W DC cable and shuts off when it is full, which fixes the 'can't recharge during a long outage' problem ChatGPT raised. Anker says most third-party portable generators can't be started this way.
standout_why: I compared against West Electric (cited), SolutionEnergy and SolarPanelX (results 13 and 14, uncited). Tesla's cited support pages returned 403 and could not be read. West Electric links generator integration only to FranklinWH and gives no specifics. SolutionEnergy describes a battery that starts a generator only for FranklinWH's installer-sold Generator Module (start at 20%, stop at 80%). For the E10 it says only that it 'can accept generator power', with no auto-start, no Smart Generator 5500, no bundle and no price. SolarPanelX doesn't mention generator recharge. ChatGPT's answer names the limitation but recommends three installer-quoted batteries (Powerwall 3, aPower 2, IQ 5P), none of which can be bought online. This isn't a 3 because a rival already has the general idea of a battery starting a generator.
kit_items: Inverter/battery: Anker SOLIX E10 Power Module + B6000 (6.144 kWh). It puts out 120/240 V split phase at 7,680 W continuous, charges from the grid at up to 7,680 W on 240 V/32 A, and expands to 30 kWh per E10.

Whole-home transfer: Anker SOLIX Power Dock. It connects to the grid at up to 200 A (160 A continuous), switches over in 20 ms or less, passes up to 24 kW from a generator, and must be installed by an electrician.

Outage recharge without solar: Anker Smart Generator 5500 (gasoline, LPG or natural gas). It delivers 4,500 W DC on gasoline or LPG and 4,000 W on natural gas, and the E10 starts it by state of charge. In the same bundle and cart.
Optional extra capacity: Anker B6000 battery module, $2,000. The owner can add it after the electrician installs the Power Dock.

Cheaper alternative that falls short: BLUETTI Apex 300 + B300K + Home Backup Kit, 5,529.6 Wh. Its rated output is 3,840 W, about half the E10's 7,680 W, and the maker pages I opened don't say it can auto-start a generator.
Amazon alternative: EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra 6 kWh + Smart Home Panel 2, about the same capacity as the base Anker kit but $500 more and no generator included.

findings.label: Battery starts the generator by state of charge
findings.value: The generator starts automatically when E10 charge reaches a threshold you set and stops when the battery is full
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX blog: automatic generator integration home battery
findings.note: Article dated 2026-08-27 and updated 2026-10-30. Quotes: 'If SOC reaches a configured threshold, Smart Generator 5500 can start automatically.' and 'E10 starts the generator when the battery drops to your set level and stops it once the battery is full' (the second is said of standby generators). Anker gives no default percentages.

findings.label: DC charge rate into E10
findings.value: 4,500 W DC (gasoline/LPG); 4,000 W (natural gas); 2 kW in Quiet mode
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX blog: automatic generator integration home battery
findings.note: Connects through 'a dedicated 4,500 W DC cable'. Runs on one fuel at a time. Arithmetic: 6.144 kWh ÷ 4.5 kW ≈ 1.4 h to refill one empty B6000, before conversion losses and before any house load being served.

findings.label: Auto-start limitation
findings.value: Most portable generators can't be started by the battery's charge level or the app
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX blog: automatic generator integration home battery
findings.note: Quote: 'most portable models lack SOC-based or app-controlled auto-start.' A standby generator must be a 240 V model with Two Wire or Utility Sensing control and no more than 24 kW surge. Anker says that while a generator runs, the battery doesn't power the home at the same time, so size the generator for the house load.
